questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'A piece of cake'
questions.x: 'A piece of cake' means: something very easy.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'Done willingly and without payment'
questions.x: 'Voluntary' means done willingly and without payment.

questions.q: Choose the option that best expresses the meaning of the idiom: 'To pull someone's leg'
o: To tease or joke with someone
questions.x: 'To pull someone's leg' means: to tease or joke with someone.

questions.q: What does the phrase 'To leave no stone unturned' mean?
questions.x: 'To leave no stone unturned' means: to try every possible means.

questions.q: Choose the word that is most nearly SAME in meaning to: DILIGENT
questions.x: 'Diligent' means hard-working. 'Careless' is close to its opposite; the others are unrelated or look-alike words.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The workers demanded / that the canteen / be opened earlier.
questions.x: The sentence is grammatically correct as written. The sentence is correct; the subjunctive 'be opened' follows 'demanded that'.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: SCANTY
questions.x: 'Scanty' is the opposite of 'Plentiful'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Scanty'.

questions.q:
Identify the segment of the sentence that contains a grammatical error. If the sentence is correct, choose 'No error'.
The committee have / submitted their report / to the Board yesterday.
questions.x: The error is in part (a): 'The committee have'. With 'yesterday', the simple past is needed: 'The committee submitted their report…'. The auxiliary 'have' (present perfect) is the error.

questions.q: Choose the one word that can be substituted for: 'That which cannot be read'
questions.x: 'Illegible' means that which cannot be read.

questions.q: Choose the word OPPOSITE in meaning to: INFERIOR
questions.x: 'Inferior' is the opposite of 'Superior'. The other options are similar in meaning to 'Inferior'.

questions.q: According to the passage, what helps a newcomer build judgement?
o: A senior colleague who explains, shares examples and admits mistakes
questions.x: Answer: 'A senior colleague who explains, shares examples and admits mistakes'. The third sentence describes the mentor's role. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Mentors shape careers more than manuals do. A new officer can read every circular and still feel lost when a real case arrives. A senior colleague who explains why rules exist, shares examples and admits past mistakes helps the newcomer build judgement. Organisations that make mentoring part of their routine, rather than leaving it to chance, retain talent and avoid repeating old errors.

questions.q: What benefit of routine mentoring is mentioned?
o: Retaining talent and avoiding old errors
questions.x: Answer: 'Retaining talent and avoiding old errors'. The last sentence lists these benefits. The other options either add ideas not found in the passage or contradict it.
questions.p: Mentors shape careers more than manuals do. A new officer can read every circular and still feel lost when a real case arrives. A senior colleague who explains why rules exist, shares examples and admits past mistakes helps the newcomer build judgement. Organisations that make mentoring part of their routine, rather than leaving it to chance, retain talent and avoid repeating old errors.

questions.q: The 'Kuka movement' in Punjab was led by:
questions.x: Correct answer: Baba Ram Singh. The Namdhari (Kuka) movement opposed British rule and cow slaughter.

questions.q: Who was the Viceroy of India at the time of the Partition of Bengal (1905)?
questions.x: Lord Curzon was Viceroy during the Partition of Bengal (1905).

questions.q: The Dandi March covered about 385 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi, ending on:
questions.x: Gandhi began on 12 March with 78 followers and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April.

questions.q: Choose the correct year for this event: Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha.
questions.x: Gandhi led the Champaran Satyagraha in 1917. Fix this date on your 1857–1947 timeline along with the events immediately before and after it.

questions.q: The 1924 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Mahatma Gandhi, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Belgaum; it was the only session presided over by Gandhi.

questions.q: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (1928) was formed at a meeting in:
questions.x: Chandrashekhar Azad and Bhagat Singh renamed the HRA, adding 'Socialist'.

questions.q: The 1929 session of the Indian National Congress, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, was held at:
questions.x: It was held at Lahore; it was the session that adopted 'Purna Swaraj' as the goal.

questions.q: Kittur Chennamma, who resisted the British in 1824, was the queen of:
questions.x: Correct answer: Kittur (Karnataka). Her revolt preceded 1857 by over three decades.

questions.q: Who founded the Swaraj Party (1923)?
o: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru
questions.x: The Swaraj Party (1923) was founded by C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru.

questions.q: The Chapekar brothers assassinated W. C. Rand in 1897 because of:
o: Excesses during plague control operations in Pune
questions.x: Correct answer: Excesses during plague control operations in Pune. It was one of the earliest political assassinations.

questions.q: The headquarters of the International Atomic Energy Agency is located in:
questions.x: International Atomic Energy Agency: headquartered in Vienna.

questions.q: Which day is observed on 8 March?
questions.x: 8 March is International Women's Day.

questions.q: At the NATO summit in The Hague (June 2025), members agreed to raise defence and security-related spending to:
questions.x: This includes 3.5% for core defence and 1.5% for related infrastructure and resilience.

questions.q: Which of the following organisations is headquartered in Geneva?
questions.x: World Health Organization is based in Geneva.

questions.q: The military exercise 'AUSINDEX' is conducted between India and:
questions.x: 'AUSINDEX' is a bilateral exercise between India and Australia.

questions.q: India's first bullet train project is being built between:
questions.x: Correct answer: Mumbai and Ahmedabad. It is being built with Japanese assistance (Shinkansen technology).

questions.q: The 'Democracy Index' is published by:
o: Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.x: 'Democracy Index' is brought out by Economist Intelligence Unit.

questions.q: Who is the Union Minister of Labour and Employment (and hence Chairman of the CBT, EPF) in the government formed in June 2024?
questions.x: Correct answer: Mansukh Mandaviya. Shobha Karandlaje is the Minister of State for Labour and Employment.

questions.q: The G20 Leaders' Summit hosted by India in September 2023 was held at:
questions.x: The theme was 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam — One Earth, One Family, One Future'.

questions.q: International Day of Yoga, proposed by India and adopted by the UN, is observed on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 21 June. It has been observed since 2015.

questions.q: "Administration of tribal areas in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram" is the subject matter of which Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.x: It is the Sixth Schedule.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Prohibition of discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 15.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle was added by the 42nd Amendment?
o: Article 39A — equal justice and free legal aid
questions.x: The 42nd Amendment added Articles 39A, 43A and 48A and amended Article 39(f).

questions.q: Who was the Chairman of the Drafting Committee of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.x: Ambedkar chaired the seven-member Drafting Committee set up on 29 August 1947.

questions.q: The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament examines:
o: Reports of the CAG on appropriation and finance accounts
Working of public sector undertakings only
questions.x: By convention it is chaired by a member of the Opposition; it has 22 members (15 LS + 7 RS).

questions.q: The Constitution (52nd Amendment) Act, 1985:
o: Gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions
Introduced the Goods and Services Tax
Added the Tenth Schedule containing anti-defection provisions
Raised the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 525 to 545
questions.x: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule containing anti-defection provisions.

questions.q: Article 352 of the Constitution of India deals with:
o: Provisions with respect to an Inter-State Council
Remedies for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (writs by the Supreme Court)
questions.x: Article 352: Proclamation of Emergency (national emergency).

questions.q: Which of the following emergencies has never been declared in India?
o: None of these — all have been declared
questions.x: Correct answer: Financial emergency (Article 360). National emergencies were declared in 1962, 1971 and 1975.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution of India provides for: "Power of the President to grant pardons, reprieves and remissions"?
questions.x: This subject is dealt with in Article 72.

questions.q: The Vice-President of India is the ex-officio Chairman of:
questions.x: Correct answer: The Rajya Sabha. Article 64.

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): Devaluation of a currency can improve the trade balance.
Reason (R): Devaluation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. Subject to elasticity conditions (Marshall–Lerner), R explains A.

questions.q: e-NAM, launched in 2016, is a:
o: Pan-India electronic trading portal networking agricultural markets
questions.x: Correct answer: Pan-India electronic trading portal networking agricultural markets. It is implemented by the Small Farmers' Agribusiness Consortium.

questions.q: Which body presents the monetary policy statement in India?
questions.x: Correct answer: Reserve Bank of India. The MPC meets at least four times a year.

questions.q: In an economy, GDP at market prices is ₹3,51,000 crore, net factor income from abroad is ₹-3,400 crore and depreciation is ₹13,000 crore. NNP at market prices is:
"Growth with stability and progressive achievement of self-reliance" was the focus of which plan?
questions.x: It was the Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969–74).

questions.q: Which committee/body is associated with "Tax reforms"?
questions.x: Raja Chelliah Committee (1991) dealt with tax reforms.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Reserve Bank of India is in:
questions.x: Correct answer: Mumbai. It was in Calcutta until 1937.

questions.q: Who is the Chief Economic Adviser who presented the Economic Surveys of 2023–24 and 2024–25?
questions.x: Correct answer: V. Anantha Nageswaran. He took charge in January 2022.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee of the RBI has how many members?
questions.x: Three from the RBI (including the Governor, who has a casting vote) and three external members.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana was launched in:
questions.x: Correct answer: August 2014. It aimed at universal access to bank accounts.

questions.q: Shares issued at a price higher than their face value are said to be issued at a:
questions.x: Securities premium is credited to Securities Premium A/c.

questions.q: Machinery costing ₹3,30,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum on the Written Down Value method. Its book value at the end of 2 years will be:
questions.x:
WDV: depreciation each year is charged on the opening book value.
Book value = Cost × (1 − r)ⁿ = 3,30,000 × (0.8)^2 = ₹2,11,200.
(SLM at the same rate would give ₹1,98,000.)

questions.q: Margin of safety is:
questions.x: It shows how much sales can fall before losses arise; MoS = Profit ÷ P/V ratio.

questions.q: Depreciation charged on machinery is recorded as:
o: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Machinery A/c Dr. To Depreciation A/c
Depreciation A/c Dr. To Cash A/c
Depreciation A/c Dr. To Machinery A/c
questions.x: Correct answer: Depreciation A/c Dr. To Machinery A/c. Depreciation is an expense; the asset value is reduced.

questions.q: Legacies received by a not-for-profit organisation are usually:
questions.x: Correct answer: Capitalised. Legacies are non-recurring receipts added to the capital fund.

questions.q: A firm has Cash ₹15,000, Debtors ₹70,000, Inventory ₹85,000, Prepaid expenses ₹10,000, Creditors ₹65,000, Bills payable ₹12,500 and Outstanding expenses ₹5,000. Its current ratio is:
'Audit trail' (edit log) in accounting software, made mandatory for companies from 1 April 2023, means:
o: A trail of physical stock movement
A record of every change made in the books of account, which cannot be disabled
questions.x: Rule 3 of the Companies (Accounts) Rules requires accounting software with an audit trail feature.

questions.q: The ledger is called the:
questions.x: Correct answer: Principal book of accounts. All accounts are maintained in the ledger.

questions.q: From the following, compute Gross Profit: Opening stock ₹55,000; Purchases ₹1,55,000; Sales ₹1,97,500; Closing stock ₹70,000.
questions.x:
Cost of goods sold = Opening stock + Purchases − Closing stock
= 55,000 + 1,55,000 − 70,000 = ₹1,40,000.
Gross profit = Net sales − COGS = 1,97,500 − 1,40,000 = ₹57,500.
Carriage inwards is a direct expense (Trading A/c).

questions.q: Purchases during a month: 1st — 150 units @ ₹18; 10th — 300 units @ ₹20; 20th — 250 units @ ₹23. 650 units were issued on the 25th. Value of closing stock under FIFO is:
questions.x: Under FIFO the earliest units are issued first, so the 50 units left come from the latest purchases: 50 × ₹23 = ₹1,150.

questions.q: Opening inventory is ₹1,00,000, closing inventory is ₹40,000 and cost of goods sold for the year is ₹2,80,000. The inventory turnover ratio is:
questions.x:
Average inventory = (1,00,000 + 40,000) / 2 = ₹70,000.
Inventory turnover = COGS / Average inventory = 2,80,000 / 70,000 = 4 times.

questions.q: Fixed costs are ₹42,000, selling price is ₹275 per unit and variable cost is ₹260 per unit. The break-even point in units is:
questions.x:
Contribution per unit = 275 − 260 = ₹15.
BEP (units) = Fixed cost / Contribution per unit = 42,000 / 15 = 2,800 units.

questions.q:
Consider the following accounts:
1. Machinery A/c
2. Goodwill A/c
3. Commission Received A/c
4. Prepaid Rent A/c
How many of the above are real accounts?
questions.x:
2 of the 4 listed items satisfy the condition asked.
Machinery and Goodwill are real accounts (tangible and intangible). Commission received is nominal; prepaid rent is representative personal.

questions.q: The cash book of a firm shows a debit (bank) balance of ₹16,000. Cheques issued but not yet presented: ₹5,500; cheques deposited but not yet credited: ₹1,000. The balance as per the pass book is:
questions.x:
Start with cash book balance ₹16,000.
+ Cheques issued not presented (bank has not yet paid) 5,500
− Cheques deposited not credited 1,000
Pass book balance = ₹20,500.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding minimum wages under the Code on Wages:
1. The Central Government fixes a floor wage which may differ for different geographical areas.
2. A State may fix a minimum wage lower than the floor wage if its cost of living is low.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is incorrect.
The floor wage may vary by geographical area, but no State can fix a minimum wage below the floor wage; if existing rates are higher they cannot be reduced.

questions.q: A factory in Pune runs with electric power and employs 18 workers. Under the OSH Code, it:
o: Is a factory because it uses power
Must obtain prior permission to retrench any worker
Is exempt from all labour laws
Is not a 'factory' (threshold is 20 with power), though other OSH provisions may apply if it has 10 or more workers
questions.x: With power the factory threshold is 20 workers, so 18 workers do not make it a 'factory'; as an establishment with 10+ workers, general OSH provisions apply.

questions.q: Under the IR Code, 'lock-out' means:
o: Refusal of workers to enter the premises
Termination of a worker for misconduct
Shifting of a factory to another State
Temporary closing of a place of employment or suspension of work by the employer
questions.x: Lock-out is the employer's counterpart of a strike — temporary closure or suspension of work or refusal to continue to employ workers.

questions.q: The Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923 was renamed the Employees' Compensation Act by an amendment in:
questions.x: The Workmen's Compensation (Amendment) Act, 2009 renamed it the Employees' Compensation Act with effect from 2010 and made it gender-neutral.

questions.q: International Workers' Day (May Day) was first celebrated in India in 1923 at:
questions.x: Singaravelu Chettiar organised the first May Day celebration in Madras in 1923.

questions.q: The World Day Against Child Labour, launched by the ILO, is observed on:
questions.x: The ILO launched the day in 2002; it is observed on 12 June.

questions.q: Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, Chapter V-B (prior permission for lay-off, retrenchment, closure) originally applied to establishments with 300 workers, later reduced in 1982 to:
questions.x: The 1982 amendment lowered the Chapter V-B threshold to 100; the IR Code restored it to 300.

questions.q: The Minimum Wages Act, 1948 has now been replaced by:
questions.x: The Minimum Wages Act is one of the four laws subsumed into the Code on Wages.

questions.q: The Pradhan Mantri Rojgar Protsahan Yojana (PMRPY), launched in 2016, incentivised employers to create new jobs by:
o: Granting tax holidays for ten years
Government paying the employer's EPS contribution (later full employer EPF contribution) for new employees
questions.x: Under PMRPY, the government paid the employer's 8.33% EPS share (from 2018, the full 12%) for new employees earning up to ₹15,000.

questions.q: Who chaired the Second National Commission on Labour that submitted its report in 2002?
questions.x: Ravindra Varma chaired the Second NCL (1999–2002). Gajendragadkar chaired the First NCL (1966–69).

questions.q:
Consider the following:
Assertion (A): The IR Code raised the threshold for applicability of standing orders from 100 to 300 workers.
Reason (R): The Code aims to give establishments greater flexibility while model standing orders protect workers.
Select the correct answer:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.x: A is true and R is true; R correctly explains A. The higher threshold was part of the flexibility-cum-protection approach of the Code; model standing orders fill gaps.

questions.q: The term 'collective bargaining' was coined by:
questions.x: Beatrice Webb (Potter) coined the term in the 1890s; the Webbs' 'Industrial Democracy' (1897) analysed it.

questions.q: The 'right to livelihood' was held to be part of the right to life under Article 21 in:
o: Kharak Singh v. State of U.P. (1962)
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950)
Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985)
questions.x: Olga Tellis (pavement dwellers' case) held that deprivation of livelihood affects the right to life.

questions.q: Which body advises the Central Government on matters dealt with in the OSH Code?
o: National Occupational Safety and Health Advisory Board
questions.x: A tripartite National OSH Advisory Board replaces multiple boards under the earlier Acts.

questions.q: Under the Code on Wages, who is responsible for paying wages to employees in an establishment?
questions.x: The employer is primarily responsible for timely payment of wages; where a contractor fails, the principal employer may be made liable to pay.

questions.q: Article 41 of the Constitution directs the State to provide public assistance in cases of:
o: Unemployment, old age, sickness and disablement
questions.x: Article 41: right to work, education and public assistance in unemployment, old age, sickness, disablement and undeserved want — the constitutional basis of social security.

questions.q: An insured employee earns gross wages of ₹20,000 in a month. What is the total ESI contribution (employer + employee) payable for that month?
questions.x:
Employee share 0.75% = ₹150 → ₹150; employer share 3.25% = ₹650 → ₹650 (rounded up to the next rupee).
Total = ₹800 (4% of wages; rates in force since 1 July 2019).

questions.q: The EPF member e-Sewa portal and UMANG allow members to activate which number to access services?
questions.x: UAN activation is the first step to accessing online EPF services.

questions.q: The insurance cover year of PMJJBY and PMSBY runs from:
questions.x: Both schemes have a cover period of 1 June to 31 May.

questions.q: The entry age for Atal Pension Yojana is:
questions.x: Subscribers must join between 18 and 40 years and contribute until 60.

questions.q: The EPF & MP Act extends to:
o: All States except Jammu and Kashmir permanently
questions.x: After the reorganisation of Jammu and Kashmir in 2019, the Act extends to the whole of India.

questions.q: The Employees' Pension Scheme came into force on:
questions.x: Correct answer: 16 November 1995. EPS 1995 replaced the Employees' Family Pension Scheme, 1971.

questions.q: Interest on EPF accumulations is credited to members' accounts:
o: Annually, on the monthly running balance
Only at the time of final settlement
questions.x: Interest is calculated on the monthly running balance and credited at the end of the financial year (and at settlement).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about ESIC:
1. It runs its own hospitals and dispensaries, besides tie-ups with other providers.
2. It runs medical colleges.
3. Its medical benefit is administered by State Governments in most States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.x:
Statement 1 is correct; Statement 2 is correct; Statement 3 is correct.
ESIC runs hospitals, dispensaries and medical colleges; medical benefit in most States is administered by the State ESI medical schemes, with ESIC-run hospitals as well.

questions.q: Submitting Form 15G/15H with an EPF withdrawal claim helps a member to:
o: Avoid TDS if total income is below the taxable limit
questions.x: Forms 15G (below 60) and 15H (senior citizens) declare that income is below taxable limit so TDS is not deducted.

questions.q: Who pays for the EDLI cover of an EPF member?
questions.x: The employer pays 0.5% of wages; members get the life cover free of cost.

questions.q: An eligible employee earns ₹17,500 per month. The notified minimum wage for the employment is ₹6,500 per month. If the establishment declares bonus at 8.33%, the annual bonus payable is (statutory computation):
questions.x:
For computing bonus, salary is capped at ₹7,000 or the minimum wage, whichever is higher: max(7,000, 6,500) = ₹7,000.
Salary for computation = min(17,500, 7,000) = ₹7,000.
Annual bonus = 7,000 × 12 × 8.33% = ₹6,997. Bonus must lie between 8.33% and 20%.

questions.q: Under the gratuity law, a period of maternity leave up to how many weeks counts as continuous service (as notified after 2018)?
questions.x: The 2018 amendment empowered the Centre to notify the maternity leave period counted as continuous service; it was aligned to 26 weeks.

questions.q: The chemical name/formula of 'washing soda' is:
questions.x: Washing soda = Na₂CO₃·10H₂O (sodium carbonate decahydrate).

questions.q: 'Encryption' converts data into:
o: A coded form that only authorised parties can read
questions.x: Correct answer: A coded form that only authorised parties can read. Decryption reverses the process with a key.

questions.q: Which abbreviation stands for 'Portable Document Format'?
questions.x: Portable Document Format is abbreviated as PDF.

questions.q: The SI unit of frequency is the:
questions.x: Frequency is measured in Hertzs.

questions.q: Which of the following is an output device?
questions.x: Plotters print large drawings.

questions.q: In a food chain, green plants are called:
questions.x: Correct answer: Producers. They make food through photosynthesis.

questions.q: Which of the following is a water-soluble vitamin?
questions.x: Correct answer: Vitamin C. B-complex and C are water soluble; A, D, E, K are fat soluble.

questions.q: 'Two-factor authentication' strengthens security by requiring:
o: Two different types of verification, e.g., password and OTP
Two passwords of the same type
questions.x: Correct answer: Two different types of verification, e.g., password and OTP. Factors: something you know, have or are.

questions.q: Deficiency of Vitamin C causes:
questions.x: Vitamin C deficiency → Scurvy.

questions.q: In computing, 'CPU' stands for:
questions.x: CPU = Central Processing Unit.

questions.q: Laws of motion and universal gravitation is credited to:
questions.x: Laws of motion and universal gravitation: Isaac Newton.

questions.q: The largest planet in the Solar System is:
questions.x: Correct answer: Jupiter. Saturn is known for its prominent rings.

questions.q: Find the odd one out among 182, 252, 73 and 70.
questions.x: 70, 252, 182 are all multiples of 7; 73 is not. Hence 73 is the odd one out.

questions.q: Find the compound interest on ₹29,000 for 2 years at 4% per annum, compounded annually.
questions.x:
Amount = P(1 + R/100)² = 29,000 × (1.04)² = ₹31,366.40.
CI = Amount − P = ₹2,366.40.
Check: SI for 2 years = ₹2,320; CI exceeds it by P(R/100)² = ₹46.40.

questions.q:
Claims settled (in thousand) over five years — 2020: 175  |  2021: 145  |  2022: 150  |  2023: 180  |  2024: 180.
What is the average per year over the five years?

A surveyor starts from point O and walks 24 km towards South, then turns right and walks 15 km, then turns right and walks 39 km, and finally turns left and walks 5 km. How far is the person from O and in which direction?
questions.x:
Take O as origin, North/East positive.
North–South: -24 +39 = 15 km → 15 km North.
East–West: -15 -5 = -20 km → 20 km West.
Distance = √(20² + 15²) = 25 km, towards North-West.

questions.q: The daily claims received are: 78, 60, 21, 59, 70, 45, 27, 65, 26. Their arithmetic mean is:
questions.x: Sum = 451; number of values = 9. Mean = 451/9 = 50.11.

questions.q: Two inlet pipes can fill a cistern in 18 hours and 36 hours respectively, while an outlet pipe can empty the full tank in 24 hours. If all three are opened together on an empty tank, it will be full in:
questions.x:
Take tank capacity = LCM(18, 36, 24) = 72 units.
Rates: +4, +2, −3 units/hour → net 3 units/hour.
Time = 72 / 3 = 24 hours.

questions.q: A courier van travels from town P to town Q at 34 km/h and returns along the same road at 102 km/h. The average speed for the whole journey is:
questions.x:
For equal distances, average speed = 2uv/(u + v) (harmonic mean), not (u + v)/2.
= 2 × 34 × 102 / (34 + 102) = 6936/136 = 51 km/h.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of 12^155?
questions.x:
Unit digit depends only on 2. Powers of 2 repeat with cycle 4: 2, 4, 8, 6.
155 ÷ 4 leaves remainder 3 → use position 3 of the cycle → 8.

questions.q: A rectangular plot measures 55 m by 45 m. What is the cost of fencing it at ₹15 per metre?
What is the smaller angle between the hour hand and the minute hand of a clock at 7:30?
questions.x:
Angle = |30H − 5.5M| = |30×7 − 5.5×30| = |210 − 165| = 45°.
Smaller angle = 45°.
(The minute hand gains 5.5° per minute over the hour hand.)

questions.q: A and B start a business investing ₹55,000 and ₹40,000 for a year. Out of a profit of ₹22,800, B gets:
questions.x:
Profit is shared in the ratio of capital × time.
A: 55,000×12, B: 40,000×12 → 11 : 8.
B's share = 8/19 × 22,800 = ₹9,600.

questions.q: Two fair dice are thrown together. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers shown is 11?
questions.x:
Total outcomes = 36. Pairs with sum 11: (5,6), (6,5) → 2.
P = 2/36 = 1/18.

questions.q: The daily output of a cement plant is first raised by 40% and the new value is then reduced by 40%. Compared with the original, the final value shows a:
questions.x:
Successive change formula: net % = a + b + ab/100 with a = +40, b = −40.
Net = 40 − 40 − (40×40)/100 = −16%.
An equal rise and fall always ends in a loss of (x²/100)%. So it is a 16% decrease.

questions.q: ₹19,800 is divided among three partners in the ratio 5 : 2 : 4. The largest share is:
questions.x:
Sum of ratio terms = 5 + 2 + 4 = 11.
One part = 19,800 / 11 = ₹1,800.
Largest share = 5 × 1,800 = ₹9,000.
